claim: MN 26 presents the future Buddha's going-forth against his parents' wishes, his search under teachers and his path to awakening; it anchors the renunciation sequence in an early Buddhist discourse but does not supply the complete later visual staging of a nocturnal departure on Kanthaka with Channa.
bounded_by: Textual attestation and layer distinction only; neither the discourse nor the relief independently verifies a reconstructable historical itinerary.
notes: Run24 answer to PR53's pending early-source question. Illustration ILL-KANDY-04 mixes a broadly canonical event with later biographical iconography.
